page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 8 vCPUs. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the CPU performance is generally modest. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests place the instance in the bottom 25% of performance, which is mirrored by weak Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores. However, the Passmark CPU score and extended instructions tests reach average levels. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is average, though small-block cached read bandwidth and overall Passmark memory scores fall into the bottom 25%.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is positioned as a memory-optimized resource. It is suitable for workloads that require a larger memory footprint relative to compute power, such as caching layers, Redis deployments, and lightweight database operations. However, the poor performance in single-threaded compression and medium-model LLM inference suggests it is not suited for compute-heavy or advanced AI tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores (8 vCPUs) and 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Performance benchmarks show weak single-core and multi-core CPU capabilities, alongside average large-block memory bandwidth and average Redis SET performance. This hardware profile is best suited for memory-intensive but compute-light workloads, such as caching layers, in-memory databases, and basic web serving, where high RAM capacity is prioritized over raw processing speed.
